cards.grammarNote: **der Spielstand** literally 'game-standing' (Spiel + Stand); masculine.
**der Punkt** point; plural *die Punkte*. *einen Punkt machen* = to score a point.
cards.phrase: Ich habe den entscheidenden Punkt gemacht!

cards.grammarNote: **das Spiel** game/match (from *spielen* 'to play'); *das Match* is also used.
cards.englishPhrase: We played a great match yesterday.
cards.phrase: Wir haben gestern ein tolles Spiel gespielt.

cards.grammarNote: **das Turnier** tournament. *sich anmelden* = 'to sign up' (reflexive + separable).
cards.englishPhrase: Jeffrey signed up for the local tournament.
cards.phrase: Jeffrey hat sich für das lokale Turnier angemeldet.

cards.grammarNote: **der Gegner** opponent (from *gegen* 'against'); female *die Gegnerin*.
**gewinnen** to win; irregular, past participle *gewonnen*.
cards.englishPhrase: We won the match against my brothers!
cards.phrase: Wir haben das Spiel gegen meine Brüder gewonnen!

cards.grammarNote: **verlieren** to lose; irregular, past participle *verloren*.
cards.englishPhrase: We lost, but it was a good game.
cards.phrase: Wir haben verloren, aber es war ein gutes Spiel.

cards.grammarNote: **der Schiedsrichter** referee (*Schieds-* + *Richter* 'judge'). *eine Entscheidung treffen* = 'to make a call'.
cards.englishPhrase: The referee made a bad call.
cards.phrase: Der Schiedsrichter hat eine falsche Entscheidung getroffen.

cards.grammarNote: **das Stadion** stadium; plural *die Stadien*.
cards.englishPhrase: There were thousands of people at the stadium.
cards.phrase: Im Stadion waren Tausende von Menschen.

cards.grammarNote: **der Trainer / die Trainerin** coach; *üben* = 'to practice'.
cards.englishPhrase: My coach says I need to practice my serve.
cards.phrase: Mein Trainer sagt, ich muss meinen Aufschlag üben.

cards.grammarNote: **der Meister / die Meisterin** champion/master; *die Meisterschaft* = the championship.
cards.englishPhrase: Jeffrey wants to be the pickleball champion.

cards.grammarNote: **die Mannschaft** team (esp. in sports); *das Team* is also common.
cards.englishPhrase: My team played really well today.
cards.phrase: Meine Mannschaft hat heute richtig gut gespielt.

cards.grammarNote: **der Spieler / die Spielerin** player.
cards.englishPhrase: Jeffrey is the best player on the court.
cards.phrase: Jeffrey ist der beste Spieler auf dem Platz.

cards.grammarNote: **das Unentschieden** a draw/tie; also used adverbially (*un-* + *entschieden* 'decided').
cards.englishPhrase: The game ended in a tie.

cards.grammarNote: **der Sportler / die Sportlerin** athlete; *der Athlet* for competitive athletes.
**der Sport** sport; *Lieblings-* prefixed to a noun = 'favorite ...'.
**der Wettkampf** competition (*Wett-* 'compete' + *Kampf* 'fight'); *der Wettbewerb* also.
cards.englishPhrase: The competition starts at nine in the morning.
cards.phrase: Der Wettkampf beginnt um neun Uhr morgens.

cards.grammarNote: **erzielen** to score (points/goals); *ein Tor schießen* for a goal, *punkten* for points.
cards.englishPhrase: My brother scored three points in a row.
cards.phrase: Mein Bruder hat drei Punkte hintereinander erzielt.

cards.grammarNote: **Pickleball** a loanword; used without an article when naming the sport (*Pickleball spielen*).
**der Schläger** racket/paddle/bat — the general word for any hitting implement (from *schlagen* 'to hit').
cards.englishPhrase: My paddle is red and black.
cards.phrase: Mein Schläger ist rot und schwarz.

cards.grammarNote: **der Platz** court/pitch; also 'space' or 'square'.
cards.englishPhrase: We reserved the court for two hours.
cards.phrase: Wir haben den Platz für zwei Stunden reserviert.

cards.grammarNote: **der Aufschlag** the serve; the verb is *aufschlagen* (separable).
cards.englishPhrase: Jeffrey has a very strong serve.
cards.phrase: Jeffrey hat einen sehr starken Aufschlag.

cards.grammarNote: **der Ballwechsel** rally, literally 'ball-exchange' (*Ball* + *Wechsel*).
**der Ball** ball; *ins Aus gehen* = 'to go out (of bounds)'.
cards.englishPhrase: The ball went out of bounds.

cards.grammarNote: **das Netz** net; also 'network' (*das Internet* comes from *Netz*).
**wandern** to hike; *die Wanderung* = a hike. *gern* + verb = 'to like doing'.
cards.englishPhrase: Jeffrey loves to hike in the mountains.
cards.phrase: Jeffrey wandert gern in den Bergen.

cards.grammarNote: **der Weg** path/trail/way; *der Wanderweg* = a hiking trail specifically.
cards.englishPhrase: The trail was steep but beautiful.
cards.phrase: Der Weg war steil, aber schön.

cards.grammarNote: **der Berg** mountain; *der Gipfel* = the summit/top.
cards.englishPhrase: We reached the top of the mountain.
cards.phrase: Wir haben den Gipfel des Berges erreicht.

cards.grammarNote: **der Rucksack** backpack (*Rücken* 'back' + *Sack*) — the source of English 'rucksack'.
cards.englishPhrase: My backpack has water and snacks.
cards.phrase: In meinem Rucksack sind Wasser und Snacks.

cards.grammarNote: **das Fahrrad** bicycle (*fahren* 'to ride' + *Rad* 'wheel'); often shortened to *das Rad*.
cards.englishPhrase: Jeffrey rides his bike to the park.
cards.phrase: Jeffrey fährt mit dem Fahrrad in den Park.

cards.grammarNote: **Rad fahren** to ride a bike (written as two words); *fahren* is irregular (*du fährst*).
cards.englishPhrase: I like to ride my bike on Sundays.

cards.grammarNote: **der Helm** helmet; *tragen* = 'to wear' (irregular, *du trägst*).
cards.englishPhrase: Always wear your helmet when you ride.
cards.phrase: Trag immer deinen Helm, wenn du fährst.

cards.grammarNote: **das Rennen** race (from *rennen* 'to run/race').
cards.englishPhrase: Jeffrey finished the race in first place.
cards.phrase: Jeffrey beendete das Rennen als Erster.

cards.grammarNote: **im Freien** outdoors, 'in the open'; *draußen* = 'outside' more casually.
**die Ziellinie** finish line (*Ziel* 'goal/finish' + *Linie*); *das Ziel* = the finish.
**trainieren** to work out/train; *Sport machen* = 'to exercise' colloquially.
cards.englishPhrase: Jeffrey exercises every morning before work.
cards.phrase: Jeffrey trainiert jeden Morgen vor der Arbeit.

cards.grammarNote: **sich dehnen** to stretch (reflexive); *die Dehnübung* = a stretching exercise.
cards.englishPhrase: I always stretch before a bike ride.
cards.phrase: Ich dehne mich immer vor einer Radtour.

cards.grammarNote: **schwitzen** to sweat; *der Schweiß* = the sweat (noun).
cards.englishPhrase: I sweat a lot during the tournament.
cards.phrase: Ich habe während des Turniers viel geschwitzt.

cards.grammarNote: **das Training** training; the verb is *trainieren*.
cards.englishPhrase: I trained hard all week for the tournament.
cards.phrase: Ich habe die ganze Woche hart für das Turnier trainiert.

cards.grammarNote: **die Geschwindigkeit** speed; *schnell* = 'fast' (adjective).
cards.englishPhrase: Jeffrey bikes at high speed downhill.
cards.phrase: Jeffrey fährt mit hoher Geschwindigkeit bergab.

cards.grammarNote: **müde** tired (adjective); *müde werden* = 'to get tired'.
cards.englishPhrase: Bean got tired after five minutes on the trail.
cards.phrase: Bean wurde nach fünf Minuten auf dem Weg müde.

cards.grammarNote: **die Verletzung** injury; *sich verletzen* = 'to get injured' (reflexive).
cards.englishPhrase: I hope I don't get injured during the race.
cards.phrase: Ich hoffe, ich verletze mich nicht während des Rennens.

cards.grammarNote: **das Wasser** water; *trinken* = to drink. *denk daran* = 'remember to'.
cards.englishPhrase: Remember to drink water during the hike.
cards.phrase: Denk daran, während der Wanderung Wasser zu trinken.

cards.grammarNote: **sich aufwärmen** to warm up (reflexive + separable: *wärmen ... auf*).
cards.englishPhrase: We always warm up before playing.
cards.phrase: Wir wärmen uns immer vor dem Spielen auf.

cards.grammarNote: **der Code** code; *der Quellcode* = source code. *sauberer Code* = clean code.
**programmieren** to program/code; regular verb, participle *programmiert*.
cards.englishPhrase: I like to code at night.

cards.grammarNote: **die Software** software; feminine, no plural. *bedienen* = 'to operate/use'.
cards.englishPhrase: This software is easy to use.
cards.phrase: Diese Software ist einfach zu bedienen.

cards.grammarNote: **der Ingenieur / die Ingenieurin** engineer; German drops the article for professions (*Sie ist Ingenieurin*).
**der Entwickler / die Entwicklerin** developer (from *entwickeln* 'to develop').
**der Computer** computer; *der Rechner* is the common native synonym.
**der Laptop** laptop; *mitbringen* = 'to bring along' (separable).
**die Tastatur** keyboard (from *die Taste* 'key'); *sich gut bedienen lassen* = 'to be nice to use'.
cards.englishPhrase: This keyboard is nice to use.
cards.phrase: Diese Tastatur lässt sich gut bedienen.

cards.grammarNote: **der Bildschirm** screen (*Bild* 'picture' + *Schirm*); *der Monitor* also.
**der Fehler** error/bug — the everyday word; *der Bug* is also used among developers.
cards.englishPhrase: There is a bug in the code.
cards.phrase: Es gibt einen Fehler im Code.

cards.grammarNote: **debuggen** to debug (anglicism); *Fehler suchen* = 'to look for bugs'. *gerade* = 'right now'.
**beheben** to fix/resolve (a bug); irregular participle *behoben*.
**bereitstellen** to deploy/provide (separable); developers also say *deployen*.
cards.englishPhrase: We deploy the new version today.
cards.phrase: Wir stellen heute die neue Version bereit.

cards.grammarNote: **der Server** server; *abstürzen* = 'to crash' (separable, uses *sein*: *ist abgestürzt*).
**die Datenbank** database (*Daten* 'data' + *Bank*).
**die App** app; feminine, plural *die Apps*. *beliebt* = 'popular'.
**die Website** website; *die Webseite* technically = a single web page.
**die Funktion** function/feature; *noch nicht* = 'not yet'.
cards.phrase: Diese Funktion ist noch nicht fertig.

cards.grammarNote: **das Feature** feature (anglicism, common in product talk); *die Funktion* also works.
**der Pull Request** kept in English; *überprüfen* = 'to review/check'.
**das Meeting** meeting (anglicism); *die Besprechung* is the native word.
cards.englishPhrase: We have a meeting this afternoon.
cards.phrase: Wir haben heute Nachmittag ein Meeting.

cards.grammarNote: **das Standup / das Daily** the daily meeting (both anglicisms, common in agile teams).
cards.englishPhrase: There is a standup every morning.
cards.phrase: Es gibt jeden Morgen ein Standup.

cards.grammarNote: **die Frist** deadline/time limit; *die Deadline* is also widely used.
**der Kunde / die Kundin** client/customer; *der Klient* more for legal/consulting.
**das Homeoffice** working from home (a German pseudo-anglicism); *im Homeoffice* = 'from home'.
**remote** used as-is (*remote arbeiten*); *die Fernarbeit* is the rarer native term.
**das Terminal** terminal; *die Konsole* is a synonym. *öffnen* = 'to open'.
**die Variable** variable; declined like an adjective-noun (*die Variable, der Variablen*).
**das Repository** repo (anglicism); often shortened to *das Repo*.
cards.englishPhrase: The code is in this repository.
cards.phrase: Der Code ist in diesem Repository.

cards.grammarNote: **der Branch** git branch (anglicism); *der Zweig* is the literal translation ('branch/twig').
cards.phrase: Ich habe einen neuen Branch erstellt.

cards.grammarNote: **überprüfen** to review/check; *das Review* = the code review (anglicism).
**der Test** test, plural *die Tests*; *durchlaufen* here = 'to pass/succeed'.
**das Update** update; *die Aktualisierung* is the native noun.
**kritisch** critical; adjective endings agree (*einen kritischen Fehler*, accusative masculine).
cards.phrase: Wir haben einen kritischen Fehler gefunden.

cards.grammarNote: **die Produktion** production; devs often say *auf Prod* or *die Produktivumgebung*.
**das Team** team; *die Mannschaft* is used more in sports.
**das Projekt** project; plural *die Projekte*.
**veröffentlichen** to launch/release/publish; *launchen* is the common anglicism.
cards.englishPhrase: We launch the product next week.
cards.phrase: Wir veröffentlichen das Produkt nächste Woche.

cards.grammarNote: **die Version** version; *neueste* = 'newest/latest' (superlative of *neu*).
**konfigurieren** to configure; *einrichten* = 'to set up' (separable).
cards.englishPhrase: I need to configure the server.

cards.grammarNote: **die Umgebung** environment/surroundings; *die Entwicklungsumgebung* = dev environment.
cards.englishPhrase: The dev and prod environments are different.
cards.phrase: Die Entwicklungs- und Produktivumgebung sind unterschiedlich.

cards.grammarNote: **ausführen** to run/execute (separable: *führe ... aus*); *laufen lassen* also used.
**das Log** log (anglicism), plural *die Logs*; *das Protokoll* is the native word.
**pushen** to push (git anglicism), participle *gepusht*; *hochladen* = 'to upload'.
cards.englishPhrase: I pushed the code to the repository.
cards.phrase: Ich habe den Code ins Repository gepusht.

cards.grammarNote: **die Integration** integration; *fehlschlagen* = 'to fail' (separable, uses *sein*).
**der Kommentar** comment; *hinzufügen* = 'to add' (separable: *füge ... hinzu*).
cards.phrase: Bitte füge ein paar Kommentare hinzu.

cards.grammarNote: **brauchen** to need; *benötigen* is the more formal synonym.
**erledigen** to finish/get done (a task); *fertigstellen* for completing a product (separable).

**das Handy** The everyday German word for a mobile phone — a pseudo-English word Germans coined; English speakers don't use *handy* this way.
**das Smartphone** Also common, especially for the modern touchscreen kind.
**der Laptop** Borrowed from English; masculine. *das Notebook* is also used.
**der Computer** Pronounced roughly *kom-PYOO-ter*; masculine. *der Rechner* ('the reckoner') is a common native synonym.
**der Bildschirm** Literally 'picture-screen' (*Bild* = picture + *Schirm* = screen/shield).
**die Tastatur** From *die Taste* ('key/button'); feminine.
**das Ladegerät** Literally 'charging-device' (*laden* = to load/charge + *Gerät* = device).

**der Akku** Short for *Akkumulator*; the rechargeable battery in a phone or laptop.
**die Batterie** A disposable battery (e.g. AA); don't mix them up.
**das WLAN** Pronounced *VEH-lahn*; the standard German word for wifi. Say *WLAN-Passwort* for the wifi password.
**das Internet** Almost always used with the article: *im Internet* = 'on the internet'.
cards.englishPhrase: I found it on the internet.
cards.phrase: Ich habe es im Internet gefunden.

cards.grammarNote: **die App** Borrowed from English; feminine. Plural *die Apps*.
cards.phrase: Ich habe eine neue App heruntergeladen.

cards.grammarNote: **herunterladen** Separable verb: *ich lade die Datei herunter*. In casual speech many just say *downloaden*.
**installieren** Regular verb; the past participle drops *ge-*: *installiert*.
cards.englishPhrase: I have to install the update.

cards.grammarNote: **das Passwort** Plural is irregular: *die Passwörter*.
**die Kopfhörer** Literally 'head-listeners' (*Kopf* = head + *Hörer* = listener); usually plural.
**die Kamera** Feminine; the *r* is rolled/soft. Refers to a phone camera or a standalone one.
cards.englishPhrase: This phone has a good camera.
cards.phrase: Dieses Handy hat eine gute Kamera.

cards.grammarNote: **das Foto** Note the *F* spelling in German. *ein Foto machen* = 'to take a photo'.
**aufladen** Separable verb: *ich lade mein Handy auf*. Same *laden* root as *herunterladen*.
cards.englishPhrase: I need to charge my phone.

cards.grammarNote: **die Nachricht** 'Message' in general; *die SMS* specifically for texts, *die Textnachricht* is the full term.
**die E-Mail** Feminine; pronounced like English. *eine E-Mail schreiben* = 'to write an email'.
**einschalten** Separable: *ich schalte den Fernseher ein*. Casually people also say *anmachen*.
**ausschalten** Separable: *ich schalte das Licht aus*. The casual opposite of *anmachen* is *ausmachen*.
**die Benachrichtigung** A mouthful, but the standard word; from *benachrichtigen* ('to notify').
**aktualisieren** The native verb; in tech speech many just say *updaten* (*das Update*).
**streamen** Borrowed from English; past participle *gestreamt*. *der Stream* = the stream.
cards.englishPhrase: We stream a lot of series.

cards.grammarNote: **der Kerker** dungeon/prison; *das Verlies* is a synonym (a dungeon cell).
**der Drache** dragon; a weak noun (*den Drachen* in accusative). *bewachen* = 'to guard'.
cards.englishPhrase: A huge dragon guards the treasure.
cards.phrase: Ein riesiger Drache bewacht den Schatz.

cards.grammarNote: **die Mission** mission/quest; *annehmen* = 'to accept' (separable).
**das Abenteuer** adventure; *der Abenteurer* = the adventurer.
**die Kampagne** campaign; *dauern* = 'to last'.
**der Charakter** character; *die Spielfigur* ('game figure') is also used.
cards.phrase: Ich habe einen neuen Charakter erstellt.

cards.grammarNote: **der Zauberer / die Zauberin** wizard (from *zaubern* 'to do magic'); *einen Zauber wirken* = 'to cast a spell'.
**der Krieger** warrior (from *der Krieg* 'war'); *heben* = 'to raise' (irregular, *hob*).
**der Schurke** rogue/villain; *stehlen* = 'to steal' (irregular, *stahl*).
**der Paladin** paladin; *mutig* = 'brave/courageous'.
**der Waldläufer** ranger (*Wald* 'forest' + *Läufer* 'runner') — the classic D&D translation; *der Ranger* also.
cards.englishPhrase: The ranger is skilled at archery.
cards.phrase: Der Waldläufer ist geschickt im Bogenschießen.

cards.grammarNote: **der Spielleiter** game master/DM (*Spiel* 'game' + *Leiter* 'leader'); often abbreviated SL.
cards.englishPhrase: The dungeon master described the scene.

cards.grammarNote: **der Zauber** spell/magic; *der Zauberspruch* is the full 'magic saying'. *mächtig* = 'powerful'.
**die Beschwörung** incantation/conjuration (from *beschwören* 'to conjure').
**die Magie** magic; *die Zauberei* is a synonym. *voller* = 'full of'.
cards.englishPhrase: The forest is full of magic.

cards.grammarNote: **der Zaubertrank** potion (*Zauber* 'magic' + *Trank* 'brew') — Asterix's famous word.
**das Schwert** sword; plural *die Schwerter*.
**der Schild** shield (masculine); note *das Schild* (neuter) means a 'sign' — a different word!
cards.englishPhrase: Block the attack with your shield.
cards.phrase: Blocke den Angriff mit deinem Schild.

cards.grammarNote: **die Rüstung** armor; *anlegen* = 'to put on' (separable: *legte ... an*).
**der Würfel** die/cube, plural *die Würfel*; also means 'cube' (*Zauberwürfel* = Rubik's cube).
cards.englishPhrase: There are some dice on the table.
cards.phrase: Auf dem Tisch liegen ein paar Würfel.

cards.grammarNote: **würfeln** to roll dice (a verb of its own); *du bist dran* = 'it's your turn'.
cards.englishPhrase: It's your turn to roll the dice.

cards.grammarNote: **der Treffer** hit; *kritischer Treffer* = a crit. Players also just say *ein Krit*.
**aufsteigen** to level up/rise (separable, uses *sein*); *die Stufe* = 'level'.
cards.phrase: Mein Charakter ist eine Stufe aufgestiegen.

cards.grammarNote: **die Erfahrungspunkte** experience points (*Erfahrung* 'experience' + *Punkte*); often abbreviated EP.
cards.englishPhrase: You gained a lot of experience points.

cards.grammarNote: **das Monster** monster; *das Ungeheuer* is the native synonym. *auftauchen* = 'to appear' (separable).
**der Kobold** goblin, plural *die Kobolde*; *der Goblin* also used in games. *versperren* = 'to block'.
**der Schatz** treasure; also a term of endearment ('sweetheart').
**die Karte** map/card; *die Landkarte* specifically for a map. *sich etwas ansehen* = 'to look at'.
**die Taverne** tavern; *das Wirtshaus / die Schenke* are native equivalents. *rasten* = 'to rest'.
**die Gruppe** party/group; *die Abenteurergruppe* = 'adventuring party'. *bestehen aus* = 'to consist of'.
cards.phrase: Unsere Gruppe besteht aus vier Personen.

cards.grammarNote: **verzaubert** enchanted (participle of *verzaubern* 'to enchant'); also 'charmed/delighted'.
**angreifen** to attack (separable: *greif ... an*); *der Angriff* = the attack (noun).
**fliehen** to flee; irregular (*floh, geflohen*). *beschließen* = 'to decide'.
**heilen** to heal/cure; *die Heilung* = the healing. *der Kleriker* = the cleric.
**verteidigen** to defend; *die Burg* = 'castle/fortress'.
**erkunden** to explore/scout; *die Höhle* = 'cave'. *lass uns* = 'let's'.
**die Lebenspunkte** hit/health points (*Leben* 'life' + *Punkte*); often abbreviated LP.
**der Zug** turn/move (in a game); *am Zug sein* = 'to be one's turn'.
**der Sieg** victory; *einen Sieg erringen* = 'to achieve a victory'. *der Sieger* = the winner.
cards.englishPhrase: In the end we achieved victory.
cards.phrase: Am Ende errangen wir den Sieg.

cards.grammarNote: **der Feind** enemy/foe; *der Gegner* = 'opponent' (less hostile). *näher kommen* = 'to get closer'.
**die Falle** trap; *aufpassen* = 'to watch out' (separable: *pass ... auf*).
**die Beute** loot/booty/prey (no plural); *teilen* = 'to split/share'.
**der Wirt / die Wirtin** innkeeper/landlord (from *das Wirtshaus*); *die Neuigkeiten* = 'news'.
cards.englishPhrase: The innkeeper gave us some news.
cards.phrase: Der Wirt gab uns ein paar Neuigkeiten.

cards.grammarNote: **der Bogen** bow (weapon); also 'arch' or a 'sheet' of paper. *treffen* = 'to hit' (irregular, *traf*).
cards.englishPhrase: She hit the target with her bow.
cards.phrase: Sie traf das Ziel mit ihrem Bogen.

cards.grammarNote: **die Spielsitzung** game session (*Spiel* + *Sitzung* 'session'); players also say *die Session*.
**die Regel** rule; *befolgen* = 'to follow/obey'. *das Regelwerk* = the rulebook.
**die Initiative** initiative; *die Reihenfolge* = 'the order/sequence'. *bestimmen* = 'to determine'.
**der zwanzigseitige Würfel** twenty-sided die (d20); players just say *der W20*. *die Probe* = 'the check'.
cards.englishPhrase: Use the d20 for the check.
cards.phrase: Benutze den zwanzigseitigen Würfel für die Probe.

cards.grammarNote:
**na?** An all-purpose casual opener — 'hey, how's it going?'. Often doubled: *Na, alles gut?*
**na ja** A hedging filler, like 'well...'.
**Moin** The northern German hello — used all day, not just mornings. Often doubled: *Moin Moin*.
**Grüß Gott** Literally 'greet God'; the standard hello in Bavaria and Austria. A northerner would say *Hallo* or *Moin*.
cards.englishPhrase: Hello, a table for two, please.
cards.phrase: Grüß Gott, einen Tisch für zwei, bitte.

cards.grammarNote: **tschüss** The everyday casual 'bye'. *tschüssi* is a cutesy version; *Ciao* is also common.
**geil** Extremely common slang for 'great/awesome' (*voll geil* = 'super cool'). It has a crude literal meaning, so it's informal only.
**krass** Youth slang for 'intense/wild', good or bad. As an exclamation *Krass!* = 'Whoa!'.
**Alter** Literally 'old one'; used like 'dude/man' to address a friend or express surprise. *Alter!* on its own = 'Dude!'.
**der Kumpel** A casual 'buddy/pal'. Originally a miner's term for a coworker.
cards.englishPhrase: He's an old buddy of mine.
cards.phrase: Er ist ein alter Kumpel von mir.

cards.grammarNote:
**doch** A one-word 'yes it is!' used to contradict a negative statement or question — English has no direct equivalent.
**doch** As a flavoring particle it also softens, like 'come on / after all'.
cards.englishPhrase: — You don't like it. — Yes I do!

cards.grammarNote: **mal** A flavoring particle that makes a request casual and light, like 'just' — *Komm mal her* = 'Come here (for a sec)'. Short for *einmal* ('once').
**Quatsch** 'Nonsense/rubbish'. As a reply *Quatsch!* = 'No way / don't be silly'. *Quatsch machen* = 'to fool around'.
**lecker** The everyday word for 'yummy/delicious'. *Das war lecker!* = 'That was tasty!'.
**Prost** The toast when drinking. More formally *zum Wohl* ('to your health'). Tradition says to make eye contact.
**das Bier** A cultural institution. Order *ein Bier, bitte*; a half-litre is *ein Großes*, a small one *ein Kleines*.
**die Kneipe** A neighborhood pub/bar — the informal spot for a beer, distinct from a *Bar* or *Restaurant*.
cards.englishPhrase: Shall we go to the pub?

cards.grammarNote: **das Brötchen** The breakfast roll — central to German food culture. Regional names vary: *Semmel* (south), *Schrippe* (Berlin).
**die Brezel** The classic knotted pretzel, especially Bavarian. In the south you'll hear *die Brezn*.
**Kaffee und Kuchen** The beloved afternoon ritual (~3–4 pm) of coffee with cake, roughly the German equivalent of tea time.
cards.englishPhrase: We're meeting for coffee and cake.
cards.phrase: Wir treffen uns zu Kaffee und Kuchen.

cards.grammarNote: **der Feierabend** The cherished moment work ends — no English equivalent. *Schönen Feierabend!* = 'Enjoy your evening off!'.
**das Pfand** The refundable deposit on bottles and cans; you return them to a *Pfandautomat* for the money back.
cards.englishPhrase: There's a deposit on this bottle.
cards.phrase: Auf diese Flasche gibt es Pfand.

cards.grammarNote: **die Autobahn** Germany's famous motorway network, parts of which have no general speed limit.
**die Gemütlichkeit** That warm, cozy, convivial feeling of comfort — a prized German value with no clean English word. Adjective *gemütlich*.
**die Schnapsidee** Literally a 'schnapps idea' — a ridiculous plan that sounds like it was hatched while drunk.
**pünktlich** 'On time' — punctuality is famously valued; being *pünktlich* means arriving exactly on time, not early or late.
